To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a carbon nanotube with fluxes is described by the extended massive Schwinger model, and the confinement phase is characterized by a Gell-Mann- Oakes-Renner-type relation for dark excitons, and nonlinear transport.

a Coulomb potential in one dimension leads to a confinement state, which is characterized by an infrared singularity in the propagator of the massive Schwinger mode, and that this confinement state can be probed by the optical measurement of the spectrum of the exciton and the nonlinear transport.

1) the low-energy physics of a single carbon nanotube in the presence of electric fluxes is described by a massive Schwinger model; 2) the Coulomb interaction between electrons leads to a confinement state; 3) this state is characterized by the existence of a dark exciton and nonlinear transport; 4) the dark exciton can be detected by an optical measurement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the confinement phase of the Schwinger model in carbon-nanotubes.
the study of the quantum field theory in curved space-time.
the physics of a carbon nanotube in the confinement phase and its relation to quantum field theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the confinement phase in carbon nanotubes has been discovered and characterized.
the confinement phase in carbon nanotubes is described by the extended massive Schwinger model.
confinement in carbon nanotubes is a very rich and interesting phenomenon which is worth studying.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the confinement phase of carbon nanotubes is a 3D analog of the massive Schwinger Model.
the carbon nanotube with the electric fluxes confined is the 2D analog to QCD in four dimensions.
the confinement phase in the carbon-nanotube is a 1D analog of the massive Schwinger-model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple 1D system can have a confinement phase, with many properties similar as in QCD in 3D or 4D.
confinement can occur in one dimension, even in a nonrelativistic system.
the confinement phase in 1D is much richer than the 3D case.
